data.description:
## Why
Agents read cold tabs all day, and a terminal that never got a PTY accepts a send that then vanishes. The same fleet freezes when main takes the renderer lock or formats a multi-megabyte screen read while a reader is stuck on the Ghostty mailbox. Backlog items: B010 (app half), B086, B003.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, Ghostty `26c3e499e`.

- B010 app half: autosave reaches `ghostty_surface_needs_confirm_quit` at `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:3960`, and that locks `renderer_state.mutex` on main (`ghostty/src/Surface.zig` near 967). The timer is a main-queue timer in `AppDelegate`. Astra overturned the "autosave waits on a mutex the reader still holds" story: `stream_handler.zig:131-134` unlocks before it blocks. The recorded freeze is teardown joining that blocked reader (`notes/2026-08-25-freeze-surface-deinit-deadlock.md`). This ticket stops the app from taking that mutex on the autosave and read paths. The abortable pushes are the Ghostty ticket.
- B086: `v2SurfaceReadText` in `Sources/SocketHandlers/SurfaceHandlers.swift` formats and base64-encodes inside `Task { @MainActor }` and the socket worker `semaphore.wait()`s with no timeout. `ghostty_surface_read_text` / `dumpText` locks `renderer_state.mutex` (`Surface.zig` near 1916). Under many `read-screen` callers this is the most frequent main-thread take of that mutex. Fable also notes the unresolved-target fallback at the `v2UUID(...) ?? ws.focusedPanelId` line in this function.
- B003: `Sources/GhosttyTerminalView.swift:2930` is `guard headlessStartupWindow == nil else { return }`. The window is cleared only when the view reaches a real window (near 2964). Portal churn can park the host with no window and leave the flag set, so every later start returns and the surface never gets a PTY. Queued `send` never flushes. Incident records, not second fixes: C11-130, C11-169, C11-235.
- Research: Fable §4 clusters C1 and C2, wave 3. Astra §2 on B010 and §4 cluster 4 (cold start is its own entry correction). `05-bug-reconciled.md`.

## Scope
In:
- Autosave and any other periodic main-thread liveness check read process-exited state, or another API that does not lock `renderer_state`, instead of `needs_confirm_quit` (B010 app half).
- `read_text` / `read-screen`: copy the snapshot on main, format and encode off main, and bound the worker wait so a wedged main cannot pin socket threads one by one (B086).
- Re-adopt a parked host into the bootstrap window when the flag is set and the view has no window, so a later start still runs (B003). Queued send flushes once the PTY exists.

Ride-alongs, same files, fix in this PR:
- B066: `read_text` and split still fall back to the focused tab when an explicit ref does not resolve (`SurfaceHandlers` near the read fallback and the split fallback). Close and clear already reject. Apply the existing reject helper to these two. Do not change send. Destructive verbs stay fail-closed as they are.
- B189: the socket reply is one unchecked `write` (`TerminalController` accept path does not set a send timeout; `writeSocketResponse` is a bare write). A large read can come back truncated. Loop until written or a real error, with a bound.
- B180: autosave writes window geometry to UserDefaults even when the bytes did not change (`AppDelegate` `persistWindowGeometry`). Skip the unchanged write. Compare a stable encoding.
- B042: new-workspace config copies a C struct and stores it on `GhosttyTerminalView` without owning the strings. Own the strings before deferred surface creation.
- B068: a closed runtime can be created again. Closed stays closed, including a late attach callback.
- B089: a replacement host is rejected until the area is 20% larger or the old host is gone. Same-size moves must be able to take the host.
- B175: a restored or new background terminal starts focused inside Ghostty. It should start unfocused unless it is the selected tab.
- B257: readiness is published before queued input is flushed. Ready means the queued send has been flushed or has failed visibly. c11 already queues a submit-on-flush. Do not claim that part is missing. Fix the ordering hole that is still there.

Out:
- Abortable mailbox pushes, paste atomicity, write-pool, and child shutdown. Those are the Ghostty ticket. This ticket depends on that bump.
- `read-selection` and off-main selection reads. C11-282 owns that command and says not to format scrollback.
- Starting a cold terminal from the read path when the helper already works. That is the cold-read ticket (B087). Land that first. This ticket rebases onto it and then moves formatting off main.
- B087's helper call. Do not invent a second start-and-wait.
- Parked rows. None of the IME or clipboard parked rows belong here.
- Sidebar measurement (B059) and the mount cap (B012).

## Approach
Wait for the Ghostty bump so teardown can abort a blocked push before this ticket re-parents hosts during churn. The process-exited read is safe earlier if the bump slips. Say which half landed if you split the PR. Prefer one PR.

Snapshot on the main actor in one short hop. Do the string work on the socket worker. Put a timeout on the semaphore and return a typed error. Do not call `dumpText` for the whole format while holding the renderer mutex on main.

For the cold host, clear or replace a bootstrap window that no longer holds the view, then start. Do not force synchronous layout to cure a blank view. Portal `bind` already has a separate layout ride-along (B049) on the tier-2 sweep. Leave it there.

`v2RejectUnresolvedTargetRefs` already exists. Use it at the read and split sites. An explicit `tab:99` that is gone is an error, not the operator's current screen.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a tagged build, create a terminal with `new-surface` into an unfocused area. It gets a PTY without a human focusing it. A queued `send` shows up in the terminal. This is the C11-235 shape, and the churn shape in C11-169.
2. `read-screen` on that tab returns text. `read-screen` on a tab id that does not exist returns not-found and does not return the focused tab's text. A multi-megabyte scrollback read returns the text, and main is not inside the format for the whole call. If main is wedged, the caller gets the timeout error instead of a stuck worker.
3. Leave a 40-tab session up across several autosave intervals with terminals still printing. The app does not freeze, and a sample of main during an autosave is not in `needs_confirm_quit`.
4. Closing the churned tab still returns after the Ghostty ticket's shutdown bound. This ticket must not reintroduce the 2026-08-25 join.
5. An unchanged autosave does not write the same window-geometry defaults again.

## Validation
`tests_v2` against a tagged build's socket for create, send, read, and a stale ref. A computer-use pass that the new unfocused terminal is actually on screen and readable, not a zero-height pane. Builds and any soak on Atlas after C11-216. The freeze regression belongs in the C11-270 soak (streaming panes, churn, autosave). Do not build on Hyperion. No source-grep test.

## Dependencies
Depends on the Ghostty mailbox patch set. Depends on the cold-read ticket (B087) so `read_text` is not edited twice in the wrong order. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216, F2 is C11-270. The lead links those. Incident records C11-130, C11-169, and C11-235 stay open as history. This ticket is the fix.

## Risks
Deadlock: a torn screen read if the snapshot is not taken on main, or a portal reparent that frees a surface on the callback stack. Typing latency: do not add work to `forceRefresh` or `hitTest`. Main thread: the format stays off main. The short snapshot hop is the exception, with the reason in the PR. Doctrine: no tenant config writes. No new UI strings expected. Public repo: describe the stuck start and the lock, not a hang recipe.

Size: L. Tier: P0. Doctrine check: app-side only. The mailbox policy change stays in the Ghostty ticket.

data.body:
Orchestrator-resolved B086 scope: consume C11-294 ghostty_surface_try_read_text after its merge and exact GhosttyKit artifact validation. BUSY returns immediately with no allocation; our app policy is a typed busy error. OK bytes are copied on main and the native text allocation freed exactly once there; only independently owned bytes go to the worker for Swift processing/encoding.

Residual explicitly out of 1.0: full off-main native text formatting. The native formatter and byte copy remain proportional to requested text and run on main after successful try-lock acquisition. The five-second caller deadline cannot preempt a native call already running. This is bounded lock acquisition, not bounded whole-read execution and not a detached snapshot. Record acquisition, native formatting/copy and worker processing timings separately in validation.

The prior snapshot-ABI planning blocker is resolved. Only B086 waits for C11-294; remaining C11-295 work need not wait. C11-296 remains a separate PR landing before read-handler edits. No implementation or validation has been run in planning mode.

Implementation checkpoint: head bff62381ae86164e26a3c7dc0ab0b59511107d76 is pushed. All 41 targeted tests passed (26 host, 15 logic), the tagged app compiled, and fresh source review found no concrete issue in the related background-focus repair.

The forty-stream keyboard fixture found a real failure on the preceding candidate: delayed layout reactivated background portals, and an input token reached the window instead of the selected terminal. The new guard resolves selection through the owning window and discards stale background focus intent. This repair still needs exact-head runtime proof; no overall PASS or PR handoff is claimed.

Final runtime validation is queued behind the two active sandbox guests. No guest is being held by this owner while waiting. The earlier read/contention/timeout evidence is preserved separately: 2,510,542 retained Unicode bytes with parity, 68 typed BUSY responses among 100 contention reads, and a real five-second caller timeout followed by recovery without a duplicate response.

C11-295 remains in progress, clean branch pushed at d3fa43c1c8a90e2aa8bac7a587e9cc756af34fbc. No PR or overall runtime PASS yet.

The four affected socket tests passed at bff62381ae86164e26a3c7dc0ab0b59511107d76, including 2,510,542 retained UTF-8 bytes and complete framing. Its 40-stream keyboard gate still failed. One focused debugger trace identified AreaInteractionOverlayHost.apply(interaction:) calling makeFirstResponder(nil) for an already-hidden overlay when its shared stream published. The repair makes that hidden nil update a no-op.

Two targeted executable tests pass at the new head: initial/unrelated updates preserve a field editor, and an actual shown interaction restores a persistent terminal-like responder on dismissal. The earlier 41 targeted tests are retained at bff62381ae; they were not repeated. Tagged build and the failed keyboard gate are next. Prior guest was dismissed with synthesized Quit and its absence verified, then deleted. All evidence will use sanitized public copies.

Clean pushed head d3fa43c1c8a90e2aa8bac7a587e9cc756af34fbc: tagged Debug build and both affected overlay focus tests PASS. Evidence checkpoint: art_01M3Y1Z6EDRFX4KZ8RH2GE3GEZ.

The new-head keyboard workload has not run. The second-slot guest remained in OS Setup Assistant after FileVault confirmation, with the welcome screen covering the app and no usable completion control. Bounded setup attempts ended; that guest was deleted. Waiting with bounded two-minute polls for the configured image to be usable as the first guest. No test reruns or additional product edits while waiting. This is not a runtime PASS, and the ticket stays in_progress with no PR.

Next: launch the retained exact-head tagged artifact in a configured isolated guest; run only the previously failed 40-stream/100-keyboard-observation gate, preserve its result, dismiss/delete the guest, and complete the draft PR/HANDOFF if it passes. Earlier socket/native/transport evidence is labeled by its tested head in the checkpoint.

C11-295 owner validation and Validator scenario; not a release or merge verdict

Head: d3fa43c1c8a90e2aa8bac7a587e9cc756af34fbc. Base: b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35. Engine: 5830d1976eecca0d7dee202aef8fb2338d99ed6d.

Tagged Debug build and the two affected overlay focus tests pass at this clean pushed head. The previous 41 targeted tests (26 host, 15 logic) and all four real socket tests passed at bff62381ae86164e26a3c7dc0ab0b59511107d76. Suites were not repeated after the six-line overlay guard. Socket proof retained 2,510,542 UTF-8 bytes / 92,980 rows and verified full/viewport/last-N/text/base64 framing, cold input once, stale target isolation and no-focus behavior.

The forty-stream keyboard gate passed at the final head: 100 native keyboard observations over 62.53 seconds, zero misses, including workspace creation/close and switching. Return-event-to-PTY p95 38.246 ms (max 114.589 ms); Return-event-to-read-screen p95 118.200 ms (max 490.164 ms). Original build executable SHA256 7cb38df3f020e2d75b406e477ee3fe44fcce088da522a220aae160c32795c77f matches the runtime record. Synthesized event timings include polling in the read-screen metric and do not measure physical-keyboard or visible-frame latency. The fixture cleaned up successfully. A separate native text/Return proof uses a neutral prompt and cropped screenshot. A focused trace on the previous head found already-hidden interaction overlays clearing the window responder on initial/unrelated shared publications. The repair makes that branch a no-op; the targeted tests cover preserved field-editor focus and actual dismissal restoring a persistent terminal-like responder. The first new-head guest failed OS first-boot setup before workload execution and was deleted. No product runtime verdict is inferred from that setup failure.

Earlier-head runtime evidence is separately labeled: be07d1f06020510ec95fb290554d6055898073bb produced 32 OK / 68 typed BUSY reads under real contention with zero successful-read parity failures; an injected main stall returned typed timeout in 5.006817 seconds, recovered on the same connection, and emitted no duplicate frame during the following 0.3 seconds. Socket workloads on baseline and that candidate each completed 100 samples with zero misses; different loads prevent a performance-gain claim. Four shutdown cases passed, including ignored HUP/TERM, with prompt close replies separated from eventual child reaping. DEBUG evidence shows unchanged geometry writes suppressed. These are not exact-final-head reruns.

Validator scenario

1. In an isolated tagged build, keep a focused sentinel and create never-focused read-first and send-first terminal tabs. First reads complete, synthetic commands execute once, and sentinel focus stays unchanged. Select each through the UI and verify readable output and ordinary keyboard input.
2. Generate numbered Unicode scrollback with at least 2 MiB retained. Compare viewport, full history, last-N, text/base64 and complete newline-delimited response framing. Under concurrent output, typed busy is allowed; successful replies preserve parity. Native formatting and copy on main remain unbounded after try-lock acquisition.
3. Read and split using a closed UUID, unknown short reference and malformed explicit reference. Each returns not_found without using or splitting the focused sentinel.
4. Run forty streaming terminals with 100 keyboard/read observations spanning several autosave intervals, create/close a disposable workspace every tenth observation and switch out/back. Verify no lost input and no background portal reactivation; retain measured distributions and load averages separately from a full fleet-soak verdict.
5. Create at least 50 workspaces, switch among old and new workspaces, move a terminal between equally sized areas, close a cold tab before queued startup, then restart/restore the tagged build. Selected content stays readable, focus follows explicit selection, closed tabs stay closed, and PTY/input state survives permitted reparenting.
6. Observe repeated actual autosaves with unchanged geometry; geometry mutation count does not rise. Check a live shell, active command, exited child and absent native runtime against snapshot eligibility. Exercise close while children ignore HUP/TERM: measure the close reply separately from eventual child reaping and verify a surviving terminal still responds.
7. Hold a client receive buffer full and exercise partial writes, EINTR, peer close and slow progress: the total write deadline does not restart and a failed frame ends that connection. Temporarily stall main in the disposable app: caller timeout returns near five seconds, recovery succeeds, and no late duplicate frame appears.

Residual: B086 bounds lock acquisition and caller wait, not native formatting/allocation/copy after acquisition. New English keys socket.terminalRead.busy and socket.terminalRead.timeout are for the separate six-locale pass. No installed skill sync or release was performed.

Evidence: prior per-head checkpoint art_01M3Y1Z6EDRFX4KZ8RH2GE3GEZ; final-head overlay/runtime addendum accompanies this comment. Baseline UI failed at the first probe, so no matched UI performance comparison exists. The final run is a successful delivery/regression check, not a fleet-soak verdict. Remaining 50+ workspace restore and broader batch checks are specified above for the Validator.

Final evidence: art_01M3Y40AQPGR0SRWMNDNVANJV0. The UI proof area measured 824 × 648 points and was readable. Synthesized Cmd-Q followed by the Quit control dismissed the exact tagged app; process absence was verified. The isolated guest was deleted after the run. No installed skills were synced, and no merge or release was performed.

PR #530 current head is 6eaab8c580 after merging main dac4fcede0 to clear conflicts that prevented CI from starting. Conflict resolution combined appended test classes, API guidance, and runtime fixture metadata; no product-code conflict needed manual resolution. Existing tagged runtime proof remains attributed to d3fa43c1c8. Merged-head build and CI verification are running; no prior evidence is relabeled.

# C11-295 review, cycle 1 (Fable, read-only)

Head reviewed: `d3fa43c1c8a90e2aa8bac7a587e9cc756af34fbc`. Base: `b6f239bd077164d2ff2e7aa18d5464d4e885fd35`. PR #530.

## Verdict: PASS at d3fa43c1c8, with runtime proof required at the merge head before landing

The diff does what the plan and the recorded ruling say and no more. B086 is bounded lock acquisition plus off-main Swift post-processing; the PR body, the code comments, the API reference and the validation comment all say so and none claim bounded native formatting. Each incident row mapped to this ticket has a behavioral test or a tagged runtime proof. No blocking finding.

What I checked and found correct:

- **Read path (B086).** Two short main hops (resolve, capture) and a global-queue formatting step share one monotonic five-second deadline through `TerminalReadCompletion`. Main never waits on the worker, so there is no cycle with C11-294 teardown (`teardownSurface` nils the pointer on main and frees next turn; the capture hop reads the pointer on main in the same turn it uses it) or with C11-302's coalescer (untouched). A late producer cannot publish after `wait()` abandons. BUSY on any region drops already-copied Swift bytes and returns typed `busy`; OK buffers are copied then freed exactly once on main. `TerminalReadBytes.formatted` reproduces the legacy candidate scoring, merge rule, line tail and base64 byte for byte. The bridging-header mirror in `ghostty.h` matches the engine at `5830d1976e` (enum values 0..4, both try-read signatures).
- **Autosave liveness (B010).** `shouldPersistScrollbackForSessionSnapshot` now calls `hasLiveProcess`, which reads `child_exited` through `ghostty_surface_process_exited` (a plain bool read in `embedded.zig`, no renderer lock). No periodic caller of `needsConfirmClose` remains; every remaining call is an operator close path.
- **Cold host (B003/B068/B089/B175/B257).** Bootstrap window re-adoption when the host is parked; `.live` gates on start, queued start, attach and create; lease order plus current-area identity replaces the 1.2 area-gain rule; desired focus applied and queued bytes flushed before the ready post; a ready observer closing the tab is handled. Host tests cover each shape.
- **Ride-alongs.** B066 (reject helper on read and split, send untouched), B189 (nonblocking send + poll loop, single five-second budget, SIGPIPE suppressed, connection ends on transport failure, flags restored), B180 (sorted-keys encoding compared against persisted bytes), B042 (owned template, pointers rebuilt only for the synchronous create). Socketpair tests exercise real kernel backpressure, EINTR and peer close.
- **Policy.** All seven new `dlog` sites are `#if DEBUG` gated. The formatting worker drains an `autoreleasepool`; the connection thread already drained per read. No focus mutation on the read path. No source-grep tests. No home paths, emails, session ids or secrets in the diff or in the two validation artifacts (extracted and grepped).
- **Evidence.** `art_01M3Y40AQPGR0SRWMNDNVANJV0` at the exact head: 40 streams, 100 keyboard observations, zero misses, binary SHA matches the build record, `not_proven` list is honest. Contention (68 BUSY / 32 OK with parity), injected main stall (typed timeout at 5.007 s, no late frame) and the 2.51 MB framed capture are at earlier heads and are labeled as such.

## Blocking

None.

## Non-blocking

1. **PR head has moved past the reviewed head.** `6eaab8c580` merges `dac4fcede0` (main) into the branch with conflict resolutions in seven product files (`GhosttyTerminalView`, `SurfaceHandlers`, `TerminalController`, `Workspace`, `AppDelegate`, `SessionPersistence`, `TerminalTab`). I inspected the combined diff: resolutions are additive and consistent. One interaction worth knowing: main's C11-280 sets `surfaceConfig.initial_input` from the surface's own `initialInput` after this PR's `inheritedInitialInput` assignment and deliberately never inherits a prior input, and no template producer sets `initial_input`, so the inherited path is dead but harmless. The exact-head runtime proof does not cover the merge head; see "Runtime proof still required".
2. **New localization keys are not in `Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`.** `socket.terminalRead.busy` and `socket.terminalRead.timeout` fall back to their `defaultValue` at runtime, so nothing is broken, but the C11-291 translator will not find them in the catalog. Smallest fix: add the two English entries to the catalog (either in this PR or as the first step of C11-291). Also note that every other socket error message in these handlers is a bare English string; localizing only these two is a convention drift, not a defect.
3. **Reject message wording.** `v2RejectUnresolvedTargetRefs` tells read-screen and new-split callers that "destructive commands never fall back to the focused target". The code is shared and the behavior is right; the prose is now wrong for the two non-destructive verbs. Smallest fix: drop the word "destructive" from both messages.
4. **`currentAreaId()` treats a failed lookup as a foreign area.** `GhosttyTerminalView.currentAreaId()` returns nil when `AppDelegate.workspaceManagerFor(workspaceId:)` has no registered window context, and the claim then fails because `areaId != nil`. The primary window registers its context from a window-accessor callback after SwiftUI has built the hierarchy, so the first `updateNSView` of a launch-time terminal can be rejected; the next geometry callback re-resolves and claims, and the launch path in the keyboard proof worked. Consider returning `areaId` (skip validation) when the lookup cannot resolve, so a registration race cannot delay the first bind. Related: `renderedVisiblePanelIdsForCurrentLayout` returns `[]` for an unregistered workspace, which the new ownerless-workspace test codifies as intended.
5. **Lookup cost in deferred callbacks.** `currentAreaId()` runs `contextContainingWorkspaceId` (windows × workspaces) plus `paneId(forPanelId:)` (panes × tabs) on every `updateNSView`, `didMoveToWindow` and `geometryChanged`. Not on the CLAUDE.md keystroke hot paths, and the constants are small today; the Validator's 50-workspace scenario is where this would first show as resize jank.
6. **Re-adopted host keeps its last visible/active flags.** The fresh-window branch of `ensureHeadlessStartupWindowIfNeeded` calls `setVisibleInUI(false)` and `setActive(false)`; the re-adopt branch does not. A host parked from a real window carries whatever state it had. The headless window is never key so no focus leaks, and the real-window swap reconciles; mentioning it for symmetry only.
7. **Four socket tests were not rerun at the final head.** The only change between `bff62381ae` and `d3fa43c1c8` is the six-line overlay guard, so this is reasonable, but the merge head rerun below should include them.

## Runtime proof still required (Atlas, before landing)

This is a risk-list ticket; its proof must be on the exact head that merges.

- Rerun on `6eaab8c580` (or whatever head is merged): the tagged Debug build, the 40-stream / 100-observation keyboard gate with workspace churn, and the four socket tests (`test_read_screen_bounded.py` with `C11_READ_SCREEN_MIN_BYTES=2097152`, the stale-target read/split checks, cold input once, no-focus). CI `build` and `compat-tests` were still pending at review time; they must be green.
- Validator scenarios 1 through 7 in the owner's validation comment stand as written. Scenario 6 is the one that closes AC3 and AC5: a main-thread sample across several real autosave intervals with 40 printing terminals, no `needs_confirm_quit` frame on the autosave path, and a geometry mutation count that stays flat. The keyboard proof's `not_proven` list correctly says autosave count and geometry mutation count were not measured at the final head.
- Scenario 5 (50+ workspaces, same-size area move, close a cold tab before queued start, restart and restore) is the only coverage for the lease and lookup behavior under scale; items 4 and 5 above are what to watch there.

Residual, as ruled: native formatting, allocation and byte copy after a successful try-lock still run on main with no wall-time bound. Full off-main native formatting stays a 1.0 residual on this ticket.
